scene-u01-pnew1-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew1-3.text: Week 14 · KP06 The cophenetic matrix and divisive methods

scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: With tied distances, single link always gives one tree; complete link depends on which pair goes first

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: top left is the matrix of Example 13.8 (yellow marks the tied $3$); three dendrograms: single link, complete link merging $\mathbf{x}_3$ with $\{\mathbf{x}_4,\mathbf{x}_5\}$ first, and complete link merging $\mathbf{x}_2,\mathbf{x}_3$ first.

scene-u01-pnew1-135.name: text#135
scene-u01-pnew1-135.text: The complete-link tie: $\mathbf{x}_3$ to $\{\mathbf{x}_4,\mathbf{x}_5\}$ is $\max(3,2)=3$, equal to $d(\mathbf{x}_2,\mathbf{x}_3)=3$

scene-u01-pnew1-138.name: text#138
scene-u01-pnew1-138.text: Merge $\mathbf{x}_3$ with $\{\mathbf{x}_4,\mathbf{x}_5\}$ first: then $\{\mathbf{x}_1,\mathbf{x}_2\}$ merges at $4$

scene-u01-pnew1-147.name: text#147
scene-u01-pnew1-147.text: Two equally short edges are both in place at that height; complete link asks for the farthest pair, so whoever is locked in first changes later farthest distances.

scene-u01-pnew1-149.name: text#149
scene-u01-pnew1-149.text: Dendrograms computed by code for both tie orders

scene-u01-pnew2-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew2-3.text: Week 14 · KP06 The cophenetic matrix and divisive methods

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: Cophenetic distance is the height where two points first join: only $N-1$ distinct values

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: the left is the single-link dendrogram of Example 13.1 with four colors for four merge heights; each cell on the right holds the height where that pair first joins, in the same color.

scene-u01-pnew2-109.name: text#109
scene-u01-pnew2-109.text: Stricter than the triangle inequality: among the three $d_C$ of any three points, the two largest are equal.

scene-u01-pnew2-113.name: text#113
scene-u01-pnew2-113.text: $d(\mathbf{x}_1,\mathbf{x}_5)=7.433$ but $d_C=4.243$; the cophenetic correlation of $P$ and $D_C$ is $0.9277$, and closer to $1$ means a more faithful tree.

scene-u01-pnew2-115.name: text#115
scene-u01-pnew2-115.text: Matrix and correlation computed by code, checked

scene-u01-pnew3-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew3-3.text: Week 14 · KP06 The cophenetic matrix and divisive methods

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: Divisive methods cut from the whole set down: enumerating all splits explodes, so shortcuts like MacNaughton-Smith are needed

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: the left compares candidates for the first divisive cut with all pairs compared by agglomeration (log scale); the right shows three rounds of MacNaughton-Smith on the five points of Example 13.1.

scene-u01-pnew3-39.name: text#39
scene-u01-pnew3-39.text: $15$ at $N=5$, $511$ at $N=10$, over half a billion at $N=30$.

scene-u01-pnew3-40.name: text#40
scene-u01-pnew3-40.text: Derivation: $2^N$ left/right choices, minus $2$ empty sides, divided by $2$ [Added]

scene-u01-pnew3-42.name: text#42
scene-u01-pnew3-42.text: MacNaughton-Smith: move out the point least alike on average first

scene-u01-pnew3-55.name: text#55
scene-u01-pnew3-55.text: Orange: moved to $C^1$; blue: stays in $C^2$

scene-u01-pnew3-66.name: text#66
scene-u01-pnew3-66.text: "How unlike those who stay" minus "how unlike those who left"

scene-u01-pnew3-70.name: text#70
scene-u01-pnew3-70.text: It reaches $\{\mathbf{x}_1,\mathbf{x}_2\}$ and $\{\mathbf{x}_3,\mathbf{x}_4,\mathbf{x}_5\}$ in three rounds; but moved points never return, so the split with the largest $g$ is not guaranteed.
